back_focal_length_mm.definition: from the last surface vertex to the paraxial image point

total_track_mm.definition: first surface vertex to the image plane along the axis

engine_check.method: thick-lens paraxial ABCD through the committed Project's COMPOUND unit

comparison.rule: per quantity: |engine - source| <= atol + rtol * scale, with scale = |EFL| for the effective focal length and max(|BFL|, |EFL|) for the back focal length
comparison.why_this_scale: a back focal length can pass through zero, so it cannot set its own tolerance; the system focal length sets the scale of a first-order comparison, and the larger of the two covers a long back focus behind a short focal length

back_focal_length.reference: measured from the vertex of surface 21, the reference the source states; the engine's distance from the last surface is 0.351068 mm and the air-conversion offset from surface 21 to it is 6.988924 mm

f_number.definition: image-space f-number stated by the source

stop_semi_diameter_mm.definition: semi-diameter of the aperture stop the Project carries
stop_semi_diameter_mm.basis: DERIVED: the paraxial stop height of the axial ray whose entrance pupil diameter is EFL / f-number

field.definition: object-space half field angle to the edge of the image circle; the source states the full field 2w

catalog_comparisons.note: no published glass reproduces both stated constants inside the tolerance; the medium is modelled as a constant index at the stated nd and the nearest published glass is recorded for comparison only

materials.note: A medium the source names is used as published. A medium the source gives only as (nd, Vd) is the catalog glass that reproduces both constants inside nd 5e-5 and Vd 0.05, recorded with the difference; no other glass is substituted.

application_facts.note: a fixed-focus wide-angle lens for factory automation / machine vision; the source states no working distance, magnification or telecentricity

approximations.description: Surfaces 22, 23, 24, 25 are the source's parallel flat plate (the optical member PP, 'a member assumed to be various filters, cover glass, or the like') and the back space behind it; they are kept as prescribed. The source's Bf is the air-converted distance from the last lens surface (21) to the image plane, so it excludes the plate; the printed plate chain reproduces it as an air-equivalent distance to 7.3401 mm against the stated 7.34 mm, i.e. within the printed rounding.

The source's specification table prints f and Bf to 0.01 mm. Every printed digit is reproduced, and the prescription as printed gives the engine's paraxial values; the engine's f and Bf agree with the printed ones to within half a print unit (0.005 mm) in every example, which is coarser than this record's comparison tolerance (atol 1e-5 mm + rtol 1e-4). The residual is the source's own rounding, not a transcription difference.

No published catalog glass reproduces both constants of 1.52841/76.45 inside nd 5e-5 / vd 0.05, so each of those media is carried as a constant index at its source-stated nd, stated relative to air; its dispersion is not modelled and only the d-line paraxial quantities are affected by the omission.

The source states no clear aperture. Each surface's clear semi-diameter is the largest paraxial footprint of the axial marginal ray at the stated aperture and, where an object field is stated, the chief ray of the widest sampled field plus half the off-axis beam radius; a mechanical value, not a source fact.
